name: IP Scanner Heuristic JS
description: No-admin port scan for a single target IP, entirely client-side (works on www too). Five selectable techniques (Fetch, Image, Link/CSS, WebSocket, IFrame), each an honest heuristic, not a real scan - see the tool text and docs/PROGRESS.md.

ip-scanner-heuristic-ls.title: IP Scanner Heuristic JS
ip-scanner-heuristic-ls.text: Type a target IP, pick a technique, adjust the port list if needed, and run a scan. Results open in the tab on the right.

ip-scanner-heuristic-cs.title: Heuristic results
ip-scanner-heuristic-cs.text: This runs entirely in the browser (works on www too, no Administrator privileges needed), but it can't do what a real scanner does: there's no raw TCP/SYN, only a protocol-level connection attempt, so a result means 'did something answer in this style', not 'this port is open'. Browsers also hard-block a fixed list of ports (e.g. 21, 22, 23, 25, 110, 445, 6667) for any of these techniques regardless of what's really listening, so the ports field only lists ports that are actually checkable in a browser. CORS/same-origin means you can tell if/how fast something answered, never read the response content. And if this page itself is served over HTTPS, plain http://\/ws:// attempts may be mixed-content-blocked no matter the real port state - this tool matches the probe scheme to the current page's scheme to avoid that, but a file:// (or plain HTTP) page is the most reliable way to run these techniques.
